questions.q: Which report would you use to confirm every asset added during a period actually shows up as expected?
questions.explain: The asset additions report lists every asset added in a period, useful for confirming nothing fell through the cracks during posting.

questions.q: What does the reserve ledger report show?
questions.explain: The reserve ledger report ties to depreciation runs and adjustments, showing accumulated depreciation by asset.

questions.q: What makes the depreciation projection report different from the other standard reports?
options: It only shows assets that have already been retired
It forecasts future depreciation based on current setup, without running or committing anything
It can only be run once per fiscal year
It only applies to tax books
questions.explain: While other reports describe what has already happened, the depreciation projection report forecasts future depreciation for budgeting purposes without committing any transaction.

questions.q: Which report lists assets still uncapitalized and not yet depreciating?
questions.explain: The CIP report lists construction-in-process assets that are still accumulating cost but not yet depreciating, as covered in Lesson 16.

questions.q: Why do reports, rather than reviewing individual asset screens, drive most period-end review work?
options: Because individual asset screens don't exist in Oracle Fusion Assets
Because reports aggregate and filter exactly what a reviewer needs for a specific question, instead of reviewing every asset one at a time
Because reports are required by law for every transaction
Because reports automatically fix any errors they find
questions.explain: Reviewing every asset record individually isn't practical at scale; reports provide structured, filtered output built to answer a specific review question.
